work_item: B04 exact-key inner join of two strict JSON string tables through Core
source_snapshot_method: SHA-256 of the compact JSON file inventory in code-snapshot.json

tests_and_route.reason_not_executed: No test or ordinary CLI route was run in this implementation slice; verification was limited to formatting, compilation, lint, build and static diff checks.

implemented_route: apps/cli -> Engine::execute/execute_inner -> input::seal -> input::interpret -> input::structured_intent -> Intent::JsonTableInnerJoin -> ports::json_table_inner_join -> JsonTableInnerJoinReport artifact -> Core dependencies and rendered output
supported_behavior: The Japanese header JSON表を「left-key」と「right-key」で内部結合して: and strict quoted English json-table-inner-join "left-key" "right-key": select key columns from left and right string tables in a wrapper with exactly left and right fields.
Each side must use the strict JSON string-table schema with unique decoded column names, rows matching header width and only string cells.
Join keys use exact decoded string equality. Each selected key must be unique on its own side; duplicate keys suspend instead of creating ambiguous row multiplication.
Only exact key matches are emitted, in left-table row order. Output columns retain every input column in left-then-right order under left. and right. namespaces, including both key columns.
The report lists unmatched left and right keys, source row indices, full wrapper and side-table SHA-256 digests, original header ranges, and per-cell byte ranges and digests for both sides.
Each input wrapper and serialized report is bounded at 256000 bytes; each table is bounded at 4096 rows, 256 columns and 65536 cells.
known_limits: No test or ordinary CLI route was executed for this slice.
This implements inner joins only. Both key columns must be explicitly named and unique; many-to-many joins, outer joins, schema inference and nonstring cells are unsupported.
The operation performs a structural transformation only and does not infer semantic equivalence or factual truth.
